questions.subject: analog-electronics
questions.question: The cut-in voltage of diodes in the rectifier of figure shown is \(0.6\text{ V}\). Identify the correct output and input characteristic (\(V_0\text{ vs }V_{\text{1}}\))
questions.explanation: The given circuit is a precision rectifier. Case 1: \(V_{i}>0.6\,\text{V}\) Diode \(D_{2}\) is ON and diode \(D_{1}\) is OFF. The circuit behaves as an inverting amplifier with \[R_{in}=10\,\text{k}\Omega,\qquad R_{f}=10\,\text{k}\Omega\] Applying KCL at the virtual ground node, \[\frac{V_{i}-0}{10\,\text{k}\Omega} = \frac{0-V_{o}}{10\,\text{k}\Omega}\] \[V_{o}=-V_{i}\] Case 2: \(V_{i}<-0.6\,\text{V}\) Diode \(D_{1}\) is ON and diode \(D_{2}\) is OFF. The inverting terminal is at virtual ground, \[V_{-}=0\] Since \(D_{2}\) is OFF, the output terminal is isolated from the feedback path and \[V_{o}=0\] Hence, \[V_{o}= \begin{cases} -V_{i}, & V_{i}>0.6\,\text{V},\\ 0, & V_{i}<-0.6\,\text{V}. \end{cases}\] \[\boxed{\text{(d) }V_{o}=0\ \text{for}\ V_{i}<0,\;V_{o}=-V_{i}\ \text{for}\ V_{i}>0.6V}\]

questions.question: The input impedance of the emitter follower of figure shown is \(k\Omega\). \(h_{ie}=600~\Omega\), \(h_{fe}=89\).
questions.explanation:
For an emitter follower (common collector), the input impedance is \[Z_{in}=h_{ie}+(1+h_{fe})R_{E}\] Given, \[h_{ie}=600\,\Omega,\qquad
h_{fe}=89,\qquad
R_{E}=1\,\text{k}\Omega\] Substituting the values, \[Z_{in}=600+(1+89)\times1000\] \[=600+90000
=90600\,\Omega
=90.6\,\text{k}\Omega\] \[\boxed{90.6}\]

questions.question: A sequential circuit formed by two edge triggered JK flipflops is shown in figure. If the states before the arrival of a clock edge are \(Q_1 = 1 , Q_2=0\) ,the states after the arrival of the clock edge are
questions.explanation:
2-bit synchronous counter , initially holds \(Q_1 = 1 , Q_2=0\) before the arrival of a clock. From figure, \[J_1 =Q_2 \quad , \quad K_1 =1 \quad , \quad K_2 = \bar Q_1\] Since the value of \(J_2\) is not given by default, we consider \(J_2=1\) . The next state equation of JK flipflop is given by \[Q_n^+ = J \bar Q_n + \bar KQ_n\] Truth table for given counter is:
\(Q_1\)\(Q_2\)\(J_1 =Q_2\)\(K_1 =1\)\(J_2=1\)\(K_2 = \bar Q_1\)Clock\(Q_1^+\)\(Q_2^+\)
100110\(\uparrow\)01
Thus , the states after arrival of clock edge are \(Q_1 = 0\) and \(Q_2 = 1\). \[\boxed{(A) \; Q_1Q_2 = 01}\]

questions.subject: control-systems
questions.question: A synchro transmitter is used with a synchro repeater for and with a control transformer for
questions.explanation:
A synchro system consists of various configurations designed for specific functional roles in control systems:
  • Synchro Transmitter-Repeater Pair: This configuration functions as a torque transmission system. Since the repeater reproduces the angular position of the transmitter with an increased driving torque capability, it is primarily used for torque transmission and mechanical positioning amplification.
  • Synchro Transmitter-Control Transformer Pair: This configuration works as an error detector. The output from the control transformer's rotor winding is an electrical voltage proportional to the sine of the angular misalignment between the transmitter and transformer shafts, making it ideal for feedback loops.
\[\boxed{\text{amplification, error detection}}\]

questions.subject: control-systems
questions.question: A unit step is applied at \(t = 0\) to a first order system without time delay. The response has a value of \(1.264\text{ units}\) at \(t = 10\text{ mins.}\) and \(2\text{ units}\) at steady state. The transfer function of the system is
questions.note: No single correct answer in the official key
questions.explanation:
The general transfer function of a first-order system is: \(\dfrac{Y(s)}{R(s)} = \dfrac{K}{\tau s + 1}\) Given a unit step input \(R(s) = \frac{1}{s}\): \[Y(s) = \frac{K}{s(\tau s + 1)} \implies y(t) = K(1 - e^{-t/\tau})\]
  • At steady state (\(t \to \infty\)), \(y(\infty) = 2\,\text{units} \implies K = 2\).
  • At \(t = 10\,\text{mins}\), \(y(10) = 1.264\,\text{units}\):
\[1.264 = 2(1 - e^{-10/\tau}) \implies 0.632 = 1 - e^{-10/\tau}\] \[e^{-10/\tau} = 0.368 \approx e^{-1} \implies \frac{10}{\tau} = 1 \implies \tau = 10\,\text{mins}\] Substituting \(K = 2\) and \(\tau = 10\,\text{mins}\) back into the transfer function expression: \[\boxed{\frac{Y(s)}{R(s)} = \frac{2}{10s + 1}}\]

questions.subject: control-systems
questions.question: The characteristic equation of a closed loop system is \(s^2 + Ks + 4K - 1 = 0\). The system is stable for \(K\) greater than
questions.explanation:
Given characteristic equation: \[s^2 + Ks + (4K - 1) = 0\] By Routh-Hurwitz stability criterion: \[\begin{array}{c|cc} s^2 & 1 & 4K - 1 \\ s^1 & K & 0 \\ s^0 & 4K - 1 & 0 \end{array}\] For the system to be stable, all elements in the first column of the Routh array must be strictly positive:
  1. \(K > 0\)
  2. \(4K - 1 > 0 \implies K > \dfrac{1}{4}\)
\[\text{Taking the intersection of both conditions: } K > 0.25\] \[\boxed{0.25}\]

questions.subject: control-systems
questions.question: A plant is controlled by a proportional controller. If a time delay element is introduced in the loop then
questions.explanation: A pure time delay has the transfer function: \(G(s)=e^{-sT}.\) Its magnitude is \(|G(j\omega)|=1,\) while its phase is \(\angle G(j\omega)=-\omega T.\) Thus, a time delay does not affect the magnitude response but introduces additional phase lag. Consequently, the phase margin decreases, whereas the gain crossover frequency remains unchanged. \[\boxed{(D)\;\text{phase margin decreases}}\]
